ratings_why.fun: The growth shape fits the seed: soft early, Old Polh and Cloister doubling mid-game, then a Dragon or Ribica spike, with two builds that pull apart at Tier 6.
ratings_why.distinct: A counter that doubles every buff and fires when it empties is new, and lending it to the enemy as drowsiness is a fresh twist; holding still echoes Hedgerow's slot clocks.

verdict_why: Mother Ribica's copies need one rules line on goldens and triples; the rest reads and grows well.

points.text: Say whether a copy of a golden Sleeper is golden, and whether copies count towards triples. As written, copy, triple, copy the new golden can roughly triple the carry every cycle.
Say whether a Wake in a fight uses up Pool Olmling's once a turn; with the Dragon or Knight it may Wake at Start of Combat before the recruit turn.
Turns 2 to 4 have only Lamplighter to spend Rest on. A Tier 1 that gives a rested neighbour +1/+1 at End of Turn would make holding still pay from the first rounds.
The Robber-Knight's fixed 8 is huge at Tier 5 and fades by the late game; a cap tied to your tier would keep it a finisher.
Dormouse Pilgrim punishes moving anything, which fights every positional card; tie it to Sleepers you didn't move instead.

standouts.why: Cowbell Kurent turns Rest running out into a domino along the row, the Wake build's heart.
Dragon of the Springs cashes the hoard every fight without losing it, a clear late payoff.
The Robber-Knight turns your own buff resource into an enemy debuff, a real off-purpose use.

weakest.why: 1 gold for not moving is slow and clashes with repositioning.
Gift-Shop Friar is a slow economy piece at Tier 4 that the tribe's builds rarely want.
Hanging Bat is a near-vanilla body; Hunker only once rested.

flags.note: Wake builds plus Dragon or Knight Start of Combat Wakes hit 12 about every turn, and the copies feed triples of your biggest unit.
Golden copies and whether copies count towards triples aren't stated.
With The Eldest, Rest only climbs, so Dark-Sensing Olm's Attack grows without limit, and any share-based gain from another tribe doubles and compounds.
